questions.stem: A 60-year-old man was diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis. Treatment with rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol was planned. He had atrial fibrillation and was taking warfarin 5 mg PO daily and multivitamins. Investigations: INR = 2.5
questions.lead_in: What drug–drug interaction should you be most concerned about?
questions.explanation: Rifampin and warfarin The most clinically significant drug–drug interaction would be rifampin and warfarin. Rifampin induces the metabolism of warfarin thus requiring a significant increase in warfarin dose to maintain appropriate INR levels. Pyrazinamide may enhance the hepatotoxic effects of rifampin, but the rifampin and warfarin drug–drug interaction is more clinically significant.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 4 Q6

questions.question: 40. Certain infections implicate the formation of biofilms by bacterias.

parts.text: List 4 infections NOT associated with foreign material in which biofilms can be found.
b) List 2 reasons why they are resistant to treatment.
c) Give 2 mechanisms by which rifampin might increase the likelihood of cure in gram positive infections associated with biofilms

cohort_answer.text: Infections without foreign material: Dental infections (gingivitis, dental abscess); IE native valve; CF patients and PNA; Chronic otitis media; Diabetic foot ulcer. Resistance reasons: Antibiotics unable to penetrate biofilm; Bacteria may replicate more slowly/be in stationary phase and less susceptible; Biofilm matrix may complex with/deactivate drug, can be too acidic; Organisms exist in distinct populations/growth stages with heterogeneous gene expression. Rifampin mechanisms: Active against metabolically dormant Staphylococci; Penetrates biofilms efficiently (lipid soluble) producing higher intra-biofilm concentrations; Active in acid environment; Prevents biofilm formation within minutes; Different mechanism than beta-lactams (inhibits RNA synthesis), providing synergy, bactericidal.

questions.question: 46. Some drugs are given IV, others per os.

parts.text: Name 5 non-beta-lactam antibacterial agents from different classes which are so excellently bioavailable that their blood levels are as good by oral administration as they are with IV

cohort_answer.text: Linezolid; Septra; Clindamycin; Rifampin; Metronidazole; Cipro; Azithro; Moxifloxacin.

parts.text: 5 antimicrobials that are highly bioavailable (only one from each class).

cohort_answer.text: Septra, doxy, azithromycin, metro, clindamycin, moxifloxacin, fluconazole

parts.text: For the following antibiotics, provide the mechanism of interaction with tacrolimus: Cipro, Vori, Rifampin, Clarithromycin

cohort_answer.text: Ciprofloxacin: no clear known interaction (immunologic effects postulated, unlikely clinically relevant). Voriconazole: likely inhibition of CYP3A4 leading to increased tacrolimus levels. Rifampin: suspected induction of CYP3A4 leading to decreased tacrolimus levels. Clarithromycin: strong CYP3A4 inhibition leading to increased tacrolimus levels.

questions.question: A patient has a PJI infection with pseudomonas and MRSA. You decide they need a long course of therapy with linezolid, ciprofloxacin and rifampin. Their other drugs are: HCTZ, ASA, Bisoprolol, Perindopril, Calcium, Metformin, Vitamin D, Rivaroxaban, Sertraline, Vitamin B12, amlodipine. In a table, list 4 possible drug interactions, with ABx in first column, other drug in second, and interaction in 3rd.

parts.text: List 4 possible drug interactions (antibiotic, other drug, interaction)

cohort_answer.text: Rifampin-Rivaroxaban: CYP3A4 strong inducers may decrease serum concentration of rivaroxaban. Rifampin-Sertraline: CYP3A4 strong inducers may decrease serum concentration of sertraline. Rifampin-Bisoprolol/Perindopril/Amlodipine: CYP3A4 strong inducers may decrease serum concentration. Linezolid-Metformin: MAOIs may enhance hypoglycemic effect. Linezolid-Sertraline: linezolid may enhance serotonergic effect of SSRIs, risk of serotonin syndrome. Ciprofloxacin-Metformin: quinolones may enhance/diminish hypoglycemic effect. Ciprofloxacin-Calcium: multivitamins/minerals may decrease serum concentration of quinolones (polyvalent cations decrease absorption). Also caution with QT-prolonging agents.

parts.text: For each of the following state whether they will increase, decrease or have no effect on the tacrolimus level: Voriconazole, Ciprofloxacin, Clarithromycin, Rifampin

questions.model_answer: Voriconazole: increases tacrolimus level (potent CYP3A4 inhibitor). Ciprofloxacin: no significant effect on tacrolimus level. Clarithromycin: increases tacrolimus level (potent CYP3A4 inhibitor). Rifampin: decreases tacrolimus level (potent CYP3A4 inducer).

parts.text: C) Give 2 reasons that rifampin can improve the chances of antimicrobial therapy succeeding?

cohort_answer.text: Active against metabolically dormant bacteria; able to penetrate S. epidermidis biofilm and can prevent biofilm formation within minutes. In vitro, addition of rifampin to S. epidermidis and MRSA biofilm infections improved susceptibility to other antibiotics and decreased adherence of bacteria to foreign material

parts.text: D) When can you use RIF alone?

cohort_answer.text: Latent TB; Chemoprophylaxis for invasive meningococcal disease exposure; Eradicate pharyngeal carriage of group B streptococci in infants with recurrent GBS sepsis

questions.question: Interactions of tacrolimus with: Ciprofloxacin, Voriconazole, Rifampin, Clarithromycin.

parts.text: Describe the interaction of tacrolimus (a CYP3A4 substrate) with each of the listed drugs.

cohort_answer.text: Tacrolimus is a CYP3A4 substrate. Ciprofloxacin - weakly inhibits CYP3A4, may increase tacrolimus. Voriconazole - inhibits CYP3A4, increases tacrolimus. Rifampin - induces CYP3A4, decreases tacrolimus levels (strongest contraindication; rifabutin should be used instead of rifampin to avoid interaction and reduce risk of acute graft rejection). Clarithromycin (and other macrolides) - inhibits CYP3A4, increases tacrolimus.

parts.text: Describe response in Tacrolimus levels in the presence of each antibiotic: Rifampin, Clarithromycin, Fluconazole
Describe clinical toxicity that could develop with each drug combination: Gentamicin + tacrolimus; MMF + TMP/SMX

cohort_answer.text: Rifampin - induces CYP3A4, decreases tacrolimus. Clarithromycin - inhibits CYP3A4, increases tacrolimus. Fluconazole - inhibits CYP3A4, increases tacrolimus. Gentamicin + tacrolimus: no true drug-drug interaction, but both can cause nephrotoxicity. MMF + TMP/SMX: no true DDI, both can cause myelosuppression.

questions.question: Abx drug interactions. You want to start an old guy on multiple meds on linezolid, cipro, rifampin. He is currently taking ASA, calcium, bisoprolol, ramipril, metformin, rivaroxaban, sertraline, acetaminophen.

parts.text: Outline the possible drug-drug interactions with each antibiotic – (2019)

cohort_answer.text: Linezolid-sertraline (serotonin syndrome, QT prolongation); Linezolid-metformin (hypoglycemia); Cipro-calcium (impaired cipro absorption); Cipro-sertraline (QTc prolongation and TdP, did not flag in interaction checker); Cipro-ASA (decreased absorption of cipro); Cipro-metformin (hypoglycemia); Rifampin-acetaminophen (increased risk hepatotoxicity); Rifampin-bisoprolol (CYP3A4 induction, decreased bisoprolol efficacy); Rifampin-calcium (decreased rifampin absorption); Rifampin-rivaroxaban (decreased rivaroxaban efficacy)

questions.question: Describe the mechanism of: Rifampin, Isoniazid, Linezolid, Moxifloxacin, Bedaquiline.

parts.text: Rifampin
Isoniazid
Linezolid
Moxifloxacin
Bedaquiline

cohort_answer.text: Rifampin: Inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, occurring as a result of drug binding in the polymerase subunit deep within the DNA/RNA channel, facilitating direct blocking of elongating RNA. Isoniazid: Inhibits mycolic acid synthesis, interfering with cell wall synthesis, producing a bactericidal effect; also disrupts DNA, lipid, carbohydrate, and NAD synthesis/metabolism. Linezolid: Inhibits initiation of bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 23S rRNA component of the 50S ribosome (contains 5S rRNA, 23S rRNA, 34 proteins); also suppresses production of bacterial toxins such as Panton-Valentine leukocidin, alpha-hemolysin, and TSST-1. Moxifloxacin: Directly inhibits DNA synthesis; binds to DNA gyrase and DNA topoisomerase IV, generating DNA cleavage. Bedaquiline: Inhibits bacterial ATP synthase; ATP production is required for cellular energy production and its loss leads to inhibition of mycobacterial growth within hours
